intro: Runs on the kind-substrate cluster: Solo Enterprise for kagent 0.5.6 with Agent Substrate, gVisor workers, no GPU. You create everything the lab uses and Reset removes it; the default pool and the other agents on the cluster are left alone. The App tab shows the lab's pool live. Turns make short live Anthropic calls.

app.label: lab-pool, live
app.hint: The lab's workers, actors and snapshots, live.

1.title: Define a worker pool
1.say: Create a WorkerPool of two pre-warmed gVisor workers, and wait until Substrate can place actors on them.
1.point: One actor runs on a worker at a time, so two workers is two turns at once, however many agents share the pool.

blocks.title: Create lab-pool
blocks.instruction: Apply the WorkerPool, wait until it reports two replicas, and wait for its worker Deployment to roll out.
blocks.expect: The pool is applied and both worker pods are running.

blocks.title: Registered with Substrate
blocks.instruction: Wait until Substrate's api-server has both workers in its own store (running pods are not enough), then list them from kagent's substrate inventory.
blocks.expect: Both lab-pool workers are listed with their pod names and IPs.

2.title: Create an agent on the pool
2.say: Apply a SandboxAgent on lab-pool and time it to Ready: kagent renders an ActorTemplate and Substrate builds its golden snapshot.
2.point: No pod for the agent. Its golden snapshot is the starting point for every conversation.

blocks.title: Apply lab-agent
blocks.instruction: Apply the SandboxAgent and wait for Ready, which means its golden snapshot exists.
blocks.expect: lab-agent is Ready, usually in well under a second once the image is on the node.

3.title: The ActorTemplate kagent rendered
3.say: Read the ActorTemplate kagent created from the agent: a plain Kubernetes object that says exactly what Substrate will run.
3.point: Sandbox class, which workers may run it, the image, config from Secrets, the readiness check, the directory snapshots carry, and the golden snapshot.

blocks.title: The agent's ActorTemplate
blocks.instruction: List the ActorTemplates kagent created for lab-agent.
blocks.expect: One template, named lab-agent plus a hash of its shape, in the gvisor class.

blocks.title: What Substrate will run
blocks.instruction: Print the parts of the template's spec that matter: sandbox class, worker selector, image, env, readiness check and the snapshotted directory.
blocks.expect: gvisor, workers labelled lab-pool, the Go ADK image, the agent's config from Secrets, and /data carried in each snapshot.

blocks.title: Its golden snapshot
blocks.expect: Ready, with a golden actor and the location of its golden snapshot.

4.title: Add a harness to the same pool
4.say: Apply an OpenClaw AgentHarness on lab-pool. kagent gives it its own ActorTemplate and golden snapshot.
4.point: Two templates, one pool: the pool is shared capacity for anything kagent renders.

blocks.title: Apply lab-harness
blocks.instruction: Apply the AgentHarness, wait for Ready, then list every ActorTemplate that runs on lab-pool with its owner.
blocks.expect: The harness is Ready, and lab-pool carries two templates: the agent's and the harness's.

5.title: Watch the turn cycle
5.say: Send one message and watch the actor's state change, then run the same conversation in a loop and watch it on the App tab.
5.point: Resuming, Running, then Suspended again within seconds, one snapshot version higher each time. The gVisor sandbox only exists during the turn.

blocks.title: The actor's lifecycle
blocks.instruction: Open a conversation, send one message, and print each state change of its actor until it suspends.
blocks.expect: Resuming, then Running, then Suspended, with the version going up, and the reply.

blocks.title: Run it in a loop
blocks.instruction: Choose how many turns, then run them one after another in one conversation. Each turn is caught running in gVisor, then suspends. Open the App tab to watch.
blocks.expect: Every turn goes Resuming, Running, Suspended with the version climbing by four, gVisor is caught serving each, and nothing is left running at the end.

checks.label: Resume, run, suspend
checks.match: Resuming v\d+ -> Running v\d+ -> Suspended v\d+

checks.label: Nothing running afterwards
checks.match: gVisor sandboxes alive on the node: 0

6.title: Snapshot a conversation, then bring it back
6.say: Tell the agent something, look at what is left once it suspends, then ask for it back.
6.point: Between turns there is no process, only a snapshot on disk. The next turn resumes from it and the conversation carries on.

blocks.title: Tell it something
blocks.instruction: Open the lab's conversation and ask the agent to remember 4242.
blocks.expect: The actor resumes, runs, suspends, and the agent confirms 4242.

blocks.title: Nothing running, only a snapshot
blocks.instruction: Show the conversation's actor and what is on the worker node for it.
blocks.expect: The actor is Suspended, its directory is on the node, and no gVisor process is alive.

checks.label: No sandbox alive
checks.match: gVisor sandboxes alive on the node right now: 0

blocks.title: Bring it back
blocks.instruction: Ask for the number, in the same conversation.
blocks.expect: The actor resumes from its snapshot and the agent answers 4242.

7.title: Load it: concurrency is the worker count
7.say: See the limit with two workers, then scale the pool and keep it busy with many conversations at once.
7.point: The pool size is how many turns run at once. Many actors share a few workers: each is handed one for a turn and gives it back.

blocks.title: Three turns, two workers
blocks.instruction: Fire three turns at the same moment at lab-agent.
blocks.expect: Two are answered in about a second; one is refused because no worker is free.

checks.label: One refused: no free worker
checks.match: refused: substrate worker pool has no free workers

blocks.title: Scale the pool
blocks.instruction: Choose how many workers, scale lab-pool with kubectl, wait for the rollout, then wait until Substrate has registered them all.
blocks.expect: The pool scales, the worker Deployment rolls out, and every worker is listed in Substrate's inventory, usually within 20 seconds.

blocks.title: Keep it busy
blocks.instruction: Choose how many conversations and for how long. Each conversation is its own actor sending turns back to back; a refused turn is retried half a second later.
blocks.expect: Up to one running actor per worker at any moment, turns answered steadily across every conversation, a few brief refusals when all workers are busy.
